rules.title: California application screening fee cap and rules
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge an application screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs and time, capped at $30 per applicant (adjusted annually for CPI since 1998). No fee if no unit is available or will be soon; the landlord must give an itemized receipt, return unused amounts, and provide a copy of the credit report within 7 days.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.effective_date_note: Current text amended by AB 1170 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 67), effective Jan. 1, 2026; the cap and fee rules predate this amendment. The document gives no single current CPI-adjusted dollar figure.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants.
rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Civ. Code § 1950.5; the fee is not treated as security. Does not preempt rules for federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.conflict_note: No single official 2026 CPI-adjusted dollar figure is stated; the statute gives only the $30 base adjusted for CPI.

parsed.doc_summary: California Civil Code § 1950.6 (as amended by AB 1170, effective 2026-01-01) caps tenant application screening fees at actual costs and no more than $30 per applicant, adjusted for CPI. It also sets conditions on charging the fee, receipts, and refunds.
